narrative:
The model estimates an 85% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your profile that historically lead to employees departing.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this prediction were your overall years of experience, whether you have received other job offers recently, and how long you have been with this organization. 

Your six to ten years of total professional experience pushed the prediction toward leaving. While many employees predicted to stay have only one to five years of experience, your mid-level tenure aligns more with people who eventually move on. Similarly, having received other job opportunities while working here was a strong factor pulling the prediction toward departure; most employees the model expects to stay have not received such offers. Finally, your one to five years in your current role also contributed to the “will leave” outcome, as shorter tenures at the present employer are more common among those who ultimately exit.

Taken together, these elements suggest the model sees you as someone with enough experience to be attractive to other employers and who is already receiving external interest. 

The organization should discuss retention options with you, such as clearer promotion paths or adjusted responsibilities. You may want to reflect on whether your current role still aligns with your long-term goals.
